newsitem.title: USA: Digital Equipment CEO reiterates Q2 goal.
newsitem.headline: Digital Equipment CEO reiterates Q2 goal.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp Chief Executive Officer Robert Palmer on Monday reiterated the computer company's goal is to be profitable in the second, fiscal quarter ending in December.
"Our objective is to get back in the black in the current quarter," Palmer told reporters at an industry conference here "In our case...black means net (income)."
Last month, the Maynard, Mass.-based company reported a larger-than-expected first quarter loss of $66 million, in part due to a worldwide sales realignment.
Palmer declined to provide a specific forecast for the quarter.
According to First Call, analysts expect Digital to post a profit of $0.10 a share versus $0.91 in the year ago quarter.

Palmer said the company has had success in selling its 64-bit Alpha computing systems and also had success with its alliance with Microsoft Corp, setting up computer systems using Windows NT server software.
Earlier, Digital said its personal computer unit is on track to achieve breakeven results in the second quarter.
